info.title: API Evangelist Governance & Discovery API
info.description: The API Commons governance and discovery tools — lint, rule authoring (validate, test and explain rulesets), coverage, waivers, reporting, certification, agent export, pipeline audit, MCP/skill forging, consumer gating, reusability, and experience mapping, plus estate adoption (baselines, federation, code-first, fixes, style guide to ruleset, org default ruleset) — as one hosted REST API. Every endpoint runs the same engine the browser tools at apicommons.org/tools run, server-side. Discovery-grade linting is free; the capabilities that generate artifacts, certify, audit repos, or roll up across many APIs are Pro. Free tier is keyless (5 req/s, 1,000/day, one document per call). Send a Pro key in the x-api-key header to unlock the Pro endpoints, SARIF output, and bulk input. Get a key at https://api.apievangelist.com/v1/auth/login.

post.description: Lint an API artifact — OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, Arazzo, JSON Schema, APIs.json, MCP, an agent SKILL.md and more (format auto-detected) — with the OpenLint engine against the curated rule catalog. Pass your own `ruleset`, or a named `profile` (OWASP, Problem Details, FHIR, API Authorization). Paid callers with an org ruleset get it by default; `ruleset` in the response says which ran.

Check that a ruleset is valid before it is run or stored: invalid JSONPath in `given` (parsed with nimma, the engine's own parser), unknown functions the engine would otherwise skip silently, undefined `#aliases`, a missing `then`, and anything the OpenLint engine rejects. Catalog metadata OpenLint refuses on a rule (`title`, `prompt`, `x-*` …) is set aside and listed in `stripped`; the engine-ready ruleset is returned when anything was stripped.

post.description: Evaluate a JSONPath — a rule's `given` — against a document and return what it matches: pointer, path and a value preview per match. Pass `field` to see whether that field is present on each match, the way `then.field` reads it. `paths` evaluates several at once.

document.description: The API description, as YAML/JSON text or a parsed object.

post.description: Run a ruleset against fixture documents with expectations. Each case is `{ name, document, expect }`: `expect` is a list of rule codes that must fire, a `{ code: count }` map for exact counts, or `[]` for "must lint clean"; optional `forbid` lists codes that must not fire. Reports pass/fail per case and rule-logic coverage: rules no case asserts on, and rules no fixture triggers. Up to 50 cases.

The rule is looked up in the `ruleset` you pass, then the curated catalog, then OpenLint's built-in rulesets.

post.description: Adopt a ruleset on a legacy API without a wall of red. With no `baseline`, snapshot today's violations into a baseline file (JSON and YAML). With a `baseline`, reconcile a new lint against it: only NEW violations fail; fixed ones are counted so the baseline can shrink; `budget` adds a warning ceiling and per-rule no-increase. Lints `document` with your `ruleset`, your org ruleset, or the catalog — or pass `violations` from your own linter.

post.description: Run the core governance checks — lint, coverage, scorecard, PII and secret classification — across a whole set of APIs and roll them up: per-API score, grade, errors and sensitive fields, estate aggregates (average score, grade distribution, APIs with PII or secrets, strongest and weakest), and a worst-first list of what needs attention. ServiceUnavailable.description: Model-backed governance is not enabled on this deployment, or the model timed out (504).

RateLimitPolicy.description: The rate-limit policy in force for the tier that served this response, in RFC 9331 quota-policy syntax: `"quota";q=1000;w=86400, "burst";q=5;w=1` — a daily quota and a per-second burst. This is the POLICY, not a live counter: `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` are deliberately not sent, because the quota is enforced by the gateway and there is no per-key usage accounting to read. Pace against the policy, and treat a 429 as authoritative.

XRateLimitLimit.description: The daily request quota for the tier that served this response.

XRateLimitWindow.description: The quota window in seconds. Always 86400 (one day).

XRateLimitTier.description: The tier this request was served on — `free`, `pro`, `business`, `internal` or `owner`. Keyless requests are `free`; requests from an apievangelist.com origin are `internal`.
